extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners preparing design patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and quality standards for drawings or photographs submitted with a U.S. design patent application, based on MPEP 1503.02 and 37 CFR 1.84. Covers format, content, shading, line types, views, color, and how drawings relate to claims/specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing or Photograph Required For Design Patent Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Every design patent application must include either a drawing or a photograph of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The drawing or photograph constitutes the entire visual disclosure of the claim; include a drawing/photograph in every design application (MPEP 1503.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing Must Be Clear and Complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing disclosure is the most important element of the application and must be clear and complete so that nothing regarding the design sought to be patented is left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all aspects of the claimed design are unambiguous and fully shown to permit proper examination and potential enforcement (MPEP 1503.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings format: black ink on white paper / comply with USPTO standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be in black ink on white paper or in another form prescribed by the USPTO and should comply with 37 CFR 1.84 for standards of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the technical drawing standards in 37 CFR 1.84 (paper size, margins, line quality, etc.) and USPTO-prescribed formats to avoid formal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs acceptable in lieu of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs are acceptable in lieu of drawings if they clearly show the appearance of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photographs only when they clearly present the design; be aware of separate rules restricting combining photographs with drawings (see 'Drawings Must Not Combine With Photographs').

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings Must Not Combine With Photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must not be combined with photographs in the same application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If photographs are used, do not present them mixed with line drawings as a single combined disclosure (MPEP 1503.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: All views necessary to fully disclose the design must be provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide every view necessary to fully disclose the claimed design so that the visual disclosure is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough orthogonal, sectional, perspective, or detail views to remove ambiguity about the claimed design's appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading must show contours and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface shading should be used to show contours and contrast and to convey the character of surface features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shading consistently to communicate three-dimensionality and surface configuration; MPEP notes that surface shading must show character (recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken lines usage and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines may be used to show environmental structure or unclaimed subject matter, but must be clearly differentiated from solid lines; rules around broken lines include prohibitions against certain uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines only to indicate non-claimed or environmental elements and ensure they are visually distinct from solid lines. The related MPEP entry 'Broken Lines Show Visible Structure Only' is listed as prohibited—follow MPEP guidance on permissible broken-line usage (MPEP 1503.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings/photographs: permitted and conditionally required
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings or photographs are permitted for design applications and may be required when color is a feature of the claimed design or when submitted under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color is an element of the claimed design, submit color drawings or photographs as required and follow USPTO procedures for color submissions (MPEP 1503.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and specification must follow design-patent-specific form
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be in a specific form for design patents and design patent applications require certain elements (some elements similar to utility patents but with design-specific requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims and the specification to conform to MPEP 1503 and design-patent practice (e.g., claim phrasing, reliance on drawings as the visual disclosure). Consult MPEP 1503 for details.
